name: Indian Institute of Science Bangalore
description: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bangalore is India's premier research-intensive university, founded in 1909, and ranked #211 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. IISc does not operate a formal, centralized public developer portal. Its confirmable public machine-readable footprint is academic: the ePrints@IISc institutional repository (EPrints software) exposes an OAI-PMH metadata interface, and the DSpace-based ETD@IISc theses repository is likewise OAI-compliant. Individual labs and centres publish open source on GitHub (for example cni-iisc, csl-iisc, val-iisc), but there is no single official institutional GitHub org with public repositories or a documented REST API program.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay
description: The Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay), founded in 1958 and located in Powai, Mumbai, is one of India's premier engineering and research institutions, ranked #97 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer footprint is largely student- and community-driven rather than a central institutional API program: the Students' Gymkhana operates an OAuth 2.0 "Profiles" identity API, the Institute Technical Council runs an ITC Single Sign-On service, and the Central Library exposes an OAI-PMH 2.0 interface over its DSpace institutional repository. No unified central developer portal was found; access to several APIs is gated to IIT Bombay infrastructure.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
description: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) is a public technical and research university in Hauz Khas, New Delhi, an Institute of National Importance and Institution of Eminence ranked #118 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer/API footprint is modest and largely research- and student-driven rather than a centralized developer program: the Central Library runs an open DSpace 8 institutional repository exposing a DSpace REST API and an OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interface, the institute operates an OAuth 2 authentication server for campus apps, and the student DevClub maintains the IITD Connect mobile-app backend with Postman-documented endpoints. There is no unified, productized public API portal.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur
description: The Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (IIT Kanpur), founded in 1959 and located in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, is one of India's premier engineering and research institutions, ranked #263 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It does not operate a unified central developer portal; its verifiable public programmatic footprint centers on the P.K. Kelkar (PKK) Library, whose Koha integrated library system exposes a live OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata-harvesting endpoint and a Koha ILS-DI service. Administrative and academic systems such as the Pingala ERP/SIS are login-gated with no documented public API, and there is no single official institutional GitHub organization, though numerous student clubs and academic departments maintain their own GitHub orgs.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur

Its public digital footprint centers on machine-readable scholarly infrastructure rather than a formal developer program: the Central Library operates a DSpace-based Institutional Digital Repository (the first IR among the IITs) and the institute maintains an IRINS research-profile portal hosted by INFLIBNET that ingests data from ORCID, Scopus, and Crossref. Operational systems such as the ERP/SSO platform are gated to enrolled members and expose no public API documentation. No official institution-wide developer portal was found; this profile catalogs the publicly reachable, standards-based endpoints only.

name: Jar
description: Jar is a Bengaluru-based fintech company operating India's first micro-savings app, enabling tens of millions of Indians to save in 24K digital gold from as little as ₹10. The app supports daily, weekly, monthly, and instant savings mechanisms, plus a round-up feature that automatically invests spare change from everyday transactions into 99.5%+ pure digital gold held in insured vaults. Founded in 2021 by Nishchay AG (CEO) and Misbah Ashraf (CPO) under Changejar Technologies Private Limited, Jar has grown to 50+ million registered users across 12,000+ Indian zip codes. The company recently vertically integrated its gold operations, moving away from a third-party distribution model to purchase, store, and manage gold directly. Jar partners with Brink's for global custody, ICICI Lombard for insurance, Vistra as independent trustee, and BDO as statutory auditor. Adjacent products include Nek, a direct-to-consumer gold and silver jewellery brand sold via shopnek.com. Jar reached profitability in 2025 after backing from Tiger Global, Arkam Ventures, Rainfall Ventures, Yes VC, and others at a $300M+ valuation, and is preparing for an IPO. There is no public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program — Jar is a B2C consumer mobile app distributed exclusively through Apple App Store and Google Play.

The company is fully compliant with AS9100, ISO 9001, OEM requirements, and export regulations, and weaves a digital thread across its supplier networks for radical transparency. Jeh operates from both the US and India and is backed by General Catalyst and IndiGo Ventures.

Jupiter is itself not a bank — it operates as a fintech marketplace and Loan Service Provider on top of regulated partners. Federal Bank is the primary banking partner for savings, salary, and deposit products, with CSB Bank powering the Edge+ and Edge RuPay credit cards and Federal Bank the Edge Federal VISA card. Lending is provided through partners including Amica Finance Private Limited and Kisetsu Saison Finance, with mutual funds through AIAPL and digital gold through MMTC-PAMP. The product is consumer facing and distributed via the Android and iOS apps; Jupiter does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal. All integrations with banks, NBFCs, NPCI/UPI rails, card networks, and depositories are private business-to-business arrangements rather than an open API program.

Founded in 2018 by Ravish Naresh, Vaibhav Kalpe, Dhanesh Kumar, and Jaideep Poonia, its flagship Khatabook Android app lets shopkeepers and small merchants record credit transactions ("udhaar"), send free WhatsApp/SMS payment reminders, collect payments via UPI and QR codes, and generate ledger statements — replacing the paper notebook ("khata") historically used across Indian retail. The app has been downloaded over 50 million times and is offered in 13+ Indian languages. Khatabook's portfolio also includes Cashbook (cash-in/cash-out tracking), Pagarkhata/Pagarbook (staff attendance and salary management), Biz Analyst (Tally mobility for accountants, acquired in 2021 for ~$10M), and a suite of GST, EMI, income tax, payroll, and loan calculators. The company has raised roughly $190M across seed through Series C from Sequoia Capital, Tencent, DST Global, GGV Capital, Y Combinator, B Capital, Moore Strategic Ventures, and angels including MS Dhoni, valuing it around $600M. Khatabook monetizes via SMB lending tie-ups, premium business tools, and adjacent fintech distribution. The Khatabook GitHub organization (verified, owns khatabook.com) exists but has no public repositories, and the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or partner program — its surface is a consumer/SMB mobile app rather than a developer platform.

name: Niyo Solutions
description: Niyo Solutions (brand: Niyo, goniyo.com) is a Bengaluru, India based consumer fintech founded in 2015 by Vinay Bagri and Virender Bisht, focused on international travel banking and savings for Indian retail customers. Niyo is not a chartered bank; it operates as a neo-banking front end layered on partner RBI-licensed banks — DCB Bank (current flagship for the Niyo zero-forex savings + debit card), SBM Bank India (previous "Niyo Global" forex card, now wound down for new customers and operating a secured credit card variant), Equitas Small Finance Bank (salary / "Niyo Bharat" account) and IDFC FIRST Bank (earlier Niyo Global issuer) — plus card network rails (Visa, RuPay). Niyo's flagship surface is the "zero forex markup" Niyo Global / DCB Niyo Global / SBM Niyo Global Visa debit and prepaid travel cards accepted in 180+ countries, paired with a digital savings account delivered through partner banks. The company has expanded beyond cards into a full travel-banking stack including currency exchange and forex cash delivery, outbound remittance (Send Money Abroad), international flights, hotels and curated experiences, Niyo Express airport services, an international travel eSIM, travel visa assistance, travel insurance, a premium subscription tier, a student program (Niyo Scholarship, NISAP) and a DCB Niyo Secured Credit Card backed by a fixed deposit. Niyo serves over one million international travellers and has raised capital from investors including Accel, Lightrock, Beams Fintech Fund, Tencent, Horizons Ventures, Prime Venture Partners and JS Capital. There is no public REST developer API, partner banking-as-a-service surface, SDK, MCP server, or GitHub organisation — Niyo is delivered exclusively as a B2C iOS and Android mobile application with a marketing and tools website at goniyo.com.

name: Swish
description: Swish (operated by Munchmart Technologies Private Limited) is a Bengaluru-based quick-commerce food delivery startup founded in 2024 that promises meals at your door in ten minutes. It runs a full-stack, vertically integrated model — owning its neighbourhood cloud kitchens ("delight centres"), sourcing and supply chain, proprietary ordering/routing technology, and its own last-mile delivery fleet — operating dense hyperlocal clusters of roughly 1.5–2 km. The company focuses on frequent, lower-ticket occasions such as breakfast, snacks, and late-night meals, and reports around 20,000 orders a day across Bengaluru micro-markets. Swish raised a $38M Series B led by Hara Global and Bain Capital Ventures with participation from Accel, valuing it at $139M post-money and bringing total funding to about $54M. Swish is a consumer mobile-app business and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

name: Tapchief
description: Tapchief was an India-based online marketplace that connected businesses and professionals with a vetted network of freelance experts, consultants, and advisors for project-based work, on-demand consultations, and expert advice. Founded in Bengaluru and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), the platform let companies discover, book, and collaborate with independent talent across functions such as marketing, finance, product, and technology. Tapchief was acquired by Chargebee in 2021, and the tapchief.com domain is now dormant. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; probing found no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

name: TartanHQ
description: Tartan (TartanHQ) is an India-based enterprise automation and verification-infrastructure company that unifies fragmented business systems (HRIS, ERP, CRM, government/regulatory sources) behind a single set of APIs and AI agents. Its core products are HyperSync (real-time income, identity, and employment data across 80+ systems), HyperVerify (a unified suite for identity, employment, and business verification), and HyperApps (AI agents that run onboarding, underwriting, and verification workflows end to end). Tartan ships a broad verification catalog — Aadhaar, PAN, UPI, GST, ITR, bank-account, DigiLocker, employment/EPFO, address, and document-OCR checks — serving banking, lending, insurance, HR-tech, and travel customers to speed KYC/KYB, reduce fraud, and keep records continuously current. Backed by 500 Global.

name: TechProcess Payment Services
description: TechProcess Payment Services is an Indian digital-payments pioneer that has been building and operating cloud-based electronic-payment platforms since 2000, when it launched BillJunction.com, India's first electronic bill presentment and payment service. Its payment gateway supports card payments, Net-banking, NACH, NEFT/RTGS, IMPS, UPI and e-wallets for merchants across India. The business is now part of Worldline India (ePayments India), whose merchant checkout product is Paynimo, offering hosted and embeddable checkout, native mobile SDKs, and 20+ e-commerce platform plugins so developers can accept digital payments with a few lines of code. Originally a Battery Ventures portfolio company, it was acquired by Ingenico Group and folded into Worldline.

name: Tejas Networks India
description: Tejas Networks is a Bengaluru, India-based optical and data networking products company that designs, develops and manufactures telecom networking equipment for communications service providers, internet and cable operators, utilities, defence and government agencies worldwide. Its portfolio spans optical transport (DWDM/OTN), packet transport, broadband access (GPON/fiber) and wireless (4G/5G radio access) systems deployed across more than 75 countries. The company is publicly listed in India (NSE/BSE TEJASNET) and is majority owned by the Tata Group; Battery Ventures was an early institutional investor. Tejas Networks is a hardware and network-infrastructure vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal or SDK program.

name: Three Wheels United
description: Three Wheels United is a fintech-driven electric vehicle financing company in India, founded in 2017 by Cedrick Tandong, Kevin Wervenbos, and Apurv Mehra. It works to remove the financial barriers to clean mobility by providing loans for two- and three-wheeler electric vehicles — starting with auto-rickshaws — disbursed through its RBI-registered NBFC lending partner Shabri Investments Private Limited. The company pairs credit with a mobile app that helps drivers manage their loans and connect to services, and reports over 4,000 vehicles financed, 20,000+ customers served, and thousands of tonnes of CO2 reduced across Bangalore, Mumbai, and the Delhi NCR (Noida) region. It is backed by Techstars, Delta Corp Holdings, Asian Development Bank Ventures, Microsoft, and other global investors, having raised roughly $10 million in Series A funding. It is a consumer-facing lender with no public developer program, API, or SDKs.
